toegepas.voor: Anja wag by die hek met 'n blou lint wat sy nie self kan vasmaak nie.
toegepas.na: Anja wag met 'n blou lint by die hek. Sy kan dit nie self vasmaak nie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written the ribbon can be read as belonging to the gate; moving it next to Anja and splitting the sentence removes the ambiguity without changing the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'by die hek met 'n blou lint' can be read as a gate with a ribbon on it
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting the ribbon next to Anja and splitting the sentence removes the misreading, keeps the same people and actions, and gives a Grade 4 reader two short sentences; 'dit' in the next line still points to the ribbon.

toegepas.voor: en gly weg op die droë grond
toegepas.na: en gly op die droë grond uit
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Uitgly' is the usual verb for slipping and falling; 'wegly' suggests sliding away, and the separable particle belongs at the end.
toegepas.fout: 'gly weg' is unidiomatic for a person losing her footing
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Uitgly' is the usual Afrikaans verb for a person slipping, and the meaning (she slips and scrapes her knee) is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Haar knie skuur oop en die rou vel brand.
toegepas.na: Haar knie skuur oop, en die rou vel brand.
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Haar knie skuur oop' and 'die rou vel brand' each have their own subject and verb, so the AWS 2017 comma before 'en' is required.

toegepas.voor: Haar nek is nat gesweet en sy haal
toegepas.na: Haar nek is nat gesweet, en sy haal
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subjects (nek, sy).
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Haar nek is nat gesweet' and 'sy haal ... uit' have their own subjects and verbs, so the AWS 2017 comma before 'en' is required.

toegepas.voor: roep juffrou Botha haar naam en
toegepas.na: roep juffrou Botha haar naam, en
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subjects (juffrou Botha, Thandi).
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Roep juffrou Botha haar naam' and 'Thandi is terug' have their own subjects and verbs, so the AWS 2017 comma before 'en' is required.

toegepas.voor: Thandi is terug op die gras
toegepas.na: Thandi is terug op die veld
toegepas.rede_vinder: Earlier Anja sits 'in die gras' beside her, so 'terug op die gras' is unclear; 'op die veld' makes plain that she is back in the game.
toegepas.fout: 'terug op die gras' is vague, because she was already sitting on grass beside the field
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Terug op die veld' is the natural expression for returning to play, and the story already uses 'veld' for the pitch, so the intended meaning is now plain.

toegepas.voor: met twee doele teen een en sy stap
toegepas.na: met twee doele teen een, en sy stap
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subjects (span, sy).
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Haar span verloor' and 'sy stap ... uit' have their own subjects and verbs, so the AWS 2017 comma before 'en' is required.

laat_vaar.voor: Die son was nog laag oor die dakke toe Thandi
laat_vaar.na: Die son is nog laag oor die dakke wanneer Thandi
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The story is told in the present tense throughout, so the opening past tense ('was ... toe') is an inconsistent tense shift.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: A past-tense scene-setting opening before a present-tense story is accepted narrative usage, changing a story's tense is a lateral move, and 'wanneer' brings in a habitual reading that 'toe' does not have.

laat_vaar.voor: teen die skool van oorkant die groot pad
laat_vaar.na: teen die skool oorkant die groot pad
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Die skool oorkant die pad' is the natural Afrikaans phrasing; 'van oorkant' is wordy and colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die skool van oorkant die groot pad' is natural spoken Afrikaans in a story voice; the proposal only reads differently.

laat_vaar.voor: vra sy en gaan sit op haar hurke
laat_vaar.na: vra sy en gaan op haar hurke sit
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In standard written Afrikaans the second verb of 'gaan sit' goes to the end after the prepositional phrase.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Gaan sit op haar hurke' is normal Afrikaans with the phrase placed after the verb, matches 'gaan sit langs haar in die gras' earlier, and the reorder is lateral.

laat_vaar.voor: Sy spoel die skaafplek skoon met water uit 'n vol bottel.
laat_vaar.na: Sy spoel die skaafplek met water uit 'n vol bottel skoon.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The particle of the separable verb 'skoonspoel' belongs at the end of the clause; the first-aid step itself is unchanged.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: It breaks up the protected first-aid wording 'spoel die skaafplek skoon met water', and the original word order is acceptable Afrikaans.

laat_vaar.voor: druk die vel saggies droog met 'n skoon doekie
laat_vaar.na: druk die vel saggies met 'n skoon doekie droog
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The particle of the separable verb 'droogdruk' belongs at the end of the clause; the first-aid step itself is unchanged.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: This is a first-aid step and the original order, with the phrase after the particle, is acceptable Afrikaans, so a reorder only for style is not justified.

laat_vaar.voor: Sy was haar hande met seep tussen elke vinger en onder haar naels.
laat_vaar.na: Sy was haar hande met seep, ook tussen haar vingers en onder haar naels.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Tussen elke vinger' is illogical (one finger has no 'between') and the phrases hang awkwardly off 'met seep'; 'ook tussen haar vingers' reads naturally with the same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Tussen elke vinger' is established Afrikaans usage, and in a hygiene step changing 'elke' to 'haar' and adding 'ook' weakens how thorough the instruction sounds instead of fixing a fault.
